sentences.en: Yeah, I think for me it did.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我觉得对我来说是的。

sentences.en: Well, I thought it would be less of a funeral than going to a funeral home with other people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我原以为这会比去殡仪馆和其他人在一起的葬礼感觉少一点仪式感。

sentences.en: And I was going to miss that.
sentences.zh: 我本来以为会错过那种感觉。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But it turned out to be totally different.
sentences.zh: 但结果却完全不同。

sentences.en: I was sitting in my solitary silence in the dining room.
sentences.zh: 我独自坐在餐厅的寂静中。

sentences.en: And as I began to hear the story of Flora's life from people, rather just sitting back listening to a memorial service that's formal.
sentences.zh: 当我开始从人们口中听到弗洛拉一生的故事时，而不是仅仅坐在那里听一场正式的追悼会。

sentences.en: You know, speaking to people afterwards,
sentences.zh: 你知道，事后和人们交谈时，

sentences.en: many told me that this felt deeper and truer and more loving than so many of the funerals that they had been to and more revealing of Flora.
sentences.zh: 许多人告诉我，这比他们参加过的许多葬礼感觉更深刻、更真实、更充满爱，也更能展现弗洛拉的本色。

sentences.en: But one person talked about how he wished he could do his mother's funeral again.
sentences.zh: 但有个人说他希望自己能重办一次他母亲的葬礼。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I'm an only son.
sentences.zh: 我是独生子。

sentences.en: And so when my mom passed, it was like I knew she was going to pass.
sentences.zh: 所以当我妈妈去世时，我其实知道她会离开。

sentences.en: She's been sick for a while.
sentences.zh: 她已经病了一段时间了。

sentences.en: And do elements from this because so much of what we do when someone dies is set out in what we think we need to do and how the elements need to be like this.
sentences.zh: 至于其中的元素，因为当有人去世时，我们所做的大部分事情都是按照我们认为必须做的方式设定的，以及这些元素必须是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And it becomes quite rote.
sentences.zh: 这变得相当刻板。

sentences.en: But it was like, okay, did I need all the pomp and circumstance, for lack of a better word, that goes on with the actual service?
sentences.zh: 但当时我在想，我真的需要那些所谓的排场和礼节吗？那些伴随着实际仪式的繁文缛节？

sentences.en: And when I thought about it a lot last night, I said, you know, a month would have loved the way that Wayne did Flora.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我仔细想了想，我说，你知道，妈妈一定会喜欢韦恩为弗洛拉所做的一切。

sentences.en: In some ways, you know, a lot of our rituals, we'd never question.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，你知道，我们很多仪式从来不去质疑。

sentences.en: We just sort of sink into them.
sentences.zh: 我们只是沉浸其中。

sentences.en: And they become like, you know, old, worn down armchairs.
sentences.zh: 它们变得就像旧的、磨损的扶手椅一样。

sentences.en: They're really comfortable.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很舒服。

sentences.en: But in some ways, I think the discomfort of the situation and the forcing of coming up with new rituals that are meaningful means that it feels more authentic and more real.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面，我认为这种处境带来的不适，以及被迫想出有意义的新仪式，意味着它感觉更真实、更纯粹。

sentences.en: It was, to my surprise, it was very touching.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，这非常感人。

sentences.en: And I felt the spirit, the unity.
sentences.zh: 我感受到了精神，感受到了团结。

sentences.en: It was something which was almost like a magic.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种魔法。

sentences.en: Like, like, it transponded you to the different dimension.
sentences.zh: 就像，就像把你带到了另一个维度。

sentences.en: You know, and also, I just think we're at this incredible time of, like, mourning as a world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，而且我也认为我们正处于一个全球哀悼的不可思议的时期。

sentences.en: We're all grieving our lives and grieving the lives that we've had before and worried about what's going to happen in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们都在为我们的生活哀悼，为我们过去的生活哀悼，并担心未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: And we're all sort of stuck in a state of suspension.
sentences.zh: 我们都处于一种悬而未决的状态。

sentences.en: And, you know, some of the grief therapists that I talked to, the counselors, they say, like, you know, when you lose someone you love deeply, you want the world to stop.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我交谈过的一些悲伤治疗师和咨询师说，当你失去深爱的人时，你希望世界停止转动。

sentences.en: And the world has stopped.
sentences.zh: 而世界确实停止了。

sentences.en: We're all kind of, like, in this collective place of reflection.
sentences.zh: 我们都处于这种集体的反思状态中。

sentences.en: I certainly know from my work as a minister and a chaplain that often society gives you the three days to grieve and then move on.
sentences.zh: 作为一名牧师和随军牧师，我当然知道，社会通常只给你三天时间去悲伤，然后就让你继续生活。

sentences.en: But we were challenged to spend a couple of weeks thinking about how best to remember my mom.
sentences.zh: 但我们被挑战去花几周时间思考如何最好地纪念我母亲。

sentences.en: And I think that was actually a healthy element, too, that we had to pause.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上也是一个健康的因素，因为我们不得不停下来。

sentences.en: Flora's son said that because he couldn't be busy and running around doing the things he would normally do to distract himself,
sentences.zh: 弗洛拉的儿子说，因为他不能忙碌，不能像平时那样为了分散注意力而四处奔波，

sentences.en: he's just been settling in his grief and thinking about his mom in a way that perhaps he would not have been.
sentences.zh: 他只是沉浸在悲伤中，以一种他以前可能不会有的方式思考他的母亲。

sentences.en: But in this situation, that's been an upside.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，这反而是一个积极的一面。

sentences.en: There's been more time, I think, to remember and to grieve and not to kind of rush through it because you have all this other stuff to do because there isn't.
sentences.zh: 我想有更多的时间去回忆和悲伤，而不是因为有其他事情要做而匆匆忙忙，因为现在没有那些事了。

sentences.en: It's just a different kind of situation right now.
sentences.zh: 这只是现在一种不同的情况。

sentences.en: So I want to, you know, invite people to see that as an opportunity,
sentences.zh: 所以我想要邀请人们把这看作一个机会，

sentences.en: an opportunity to grieve because I think too often we just rush through those things because they're more painful and not that comfortable.
sentences.zh: 一个悲伤的机会，因为我认为我们太常匆匆略过这些事情，因为它们更痛苦，也不那么舒服。

sentences.en: I'm curious how Wayne is faring since the funeral.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇韦恩葬礼后的情况如何。

sentences.en: Have you checked in with him?
sentences.zh: 你和他联系过吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've checked in with him a few times now.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我已经和他联系过几次了。

sentences.en: I talked to him the day after.
sentences.zh: 我在葬礼后的第二天和他谈过。

sentences.en: He was very, you know, that night he watched Jesus Christ Superstar, which he said Flora did not love, but he loves it.
sentences.zh: 他当时非常，你知道，那天晚上他看了《耶稣基督万世巨星》，他说弗洛拉不喜欢这部剧，但他很喜欢。

sentences.en: He's also just been reading her poetry and going through the books of her writing and delighting in that.
sentences.zh: 他还一直在读她的诗，翻看她的写作手稿，并从中感到快乐。

sentences.en: In this time of suspension, he's using some of the time to really sink in and reflect and say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 在这个悬而未决的时期，他利用一些时间真正沉下心来反思并告别。

sentences.en: I found a book of her poetry.
sentences.zh: 我找到了一本她的诗集。

sentences.en: I think I maybe mentioned that the other day.
sentences.zh: 我想前几天我可能提到过。

sentences.en: And so I've been reading one of them each day and I read one today and it's about the Highlands in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以我每天读一首，今天读了一首，是关于苏格兰高地的。

sentences.en: And so I I'd love to read it to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我很想读给你听。

sentences.en: Can I read it to you?
sentences.zh: 我可以读给你听吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I'd love that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我太想听了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let me just go and grab the book.
sentences.zh: 让我去把书拿来。

sentences.en: I just I never read them really before.
sentences.zh: 我以前真的从来没读过它们。

sentences.en: And she just put them in a little book and it was sitting in her desk.
sentences.zh: 她把它们放在一本小书里，就放在她的书桌上。

sentences.en: And let's see, here it is called Scottish Highlands.
sentences.zh: 让我看看，这首叫《苏格兰高地》。

sentences.en: Highland of wild beauty.
sentences.zh: 狂野之美的高地。

sentences.en: In wooded places of the Glen's heart, bird and feathered creatures find a refuge near the glistening loch.
sentences.zh: 在峡谷深处的林地，鸟儿和羽毛生物在波光粼粼的湖边找到了避难所。

sentences.en: Up like a liquid silver pool within the palm, where trout can flash and play,
sentences.zh: 像掌心里的液态银池，鳟鱼在其中闪烁嬉戏，

sentences.en: while here and there a weary castle still looks down upon a pastoral scene of black and white-faced sheep without shepherd.
sentences.zh: 而这里那里，一座疲惫的城堡依然俯瞰着没有牧羊人的黑白面羊的田园风光。

sentences.en: But quiet and content beside a spreading river, where it grazed a long-horned shaggy cattle beasts.
sentences.zh: 但在蜿蜒的河流旁，宁静而满足，长角毛茸茸的牛群在那里吃草。

sentences.en: Color surprises, brightens the grassy bed with foxglove and buttercup, daisy, dog rose and iris.
sentences.zh: 色彩令人惊喜，毛地黄、毛茛、雏菊、狗蔷薇和鸢尾花点亮了草地。

sentences.en: A feast for the eyes and heart, no longer confined, but roaming wild and free in the high land.
sentences.zh: 这是眼睛和心灵的盛宴，不再受束缚，在高地上自由自在地漫游。

sentences.en: So that, I thought, that's rich.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想，这真是丰富。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: That is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这太美了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Department of Labor revealed that an additional 4.4 million Americans filed for unemployment benefits last week,
sentences.zh: 周四，劳工部透露，上周又有440万美国人申请了失业救济金，

sentences.en: bringing the total since the start of the crisis to 26 million.
sentences.zh: 使危机开始以来的总数达到2600万。

sentences.en: Economists now estimate that the national unemployment rate is between 15 and 20 percent, higher than during the deep recession that followed the 2008 financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 经济学家现在估计，全国失业率在15%到20%之间，高于2008年金融危机后的深度衰退时期。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: Today was an historic day for us to once again pass our now fourth bipartisan legislation to address the coronavirus crisis.
sentences.zh: 今天对我们来说是历史性的一天，我们再次通过了第四项应对新冠危机的两党立法。

sentences.en: We're very pleased with the vote.
sentences.zh: 我们对这次投票结果非常满意。

sentences.en: In Washington, the House of Representatives passed the $484 billion aid package, already passed by the Senate, designed to bail out small businesses, fund hospitals,
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，众议院通过了总额4840亿美元的援助方案，该方案此前已在参议院获得通过，旨在救助小企业、资助医院，

sentences.en: and expand testing for the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 并扩大新冠病毒检测范围。

sentences.en: But the bill did not include any financial assistance to states, as Democrats had demanded.
sentences.zh: 但该法案并未包含民主党人所要求的对各州的财政援助。

sentences.en: In a radio interview,
sentences.zh: 在一次广播采访中，

sentences.en: Republican Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said that states running out of money may need to consider filing for bankruptcy rather than relying on the federal government.
sentences.zh: 共和党参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔表示，资金耗尽的州可能需要考虑申请破产，而不是依赖联邦政府。

sentences.en: I would certainly be in favor of allowing states to use the bankruptcy route.
sentences.zh: 我当然支持允许各州走破产程序。

sentences.en: It saved some cities, and there's no good reason for it not to be available.
sentences.zh: 这曾挽救了一些城市，没有理由不让各州使用这一途径。

sentences.en: That drew angry reactions from both Democratic and Republican governors, including Jay Inslee of Washington State, who appeared on ABC.
sentences.zh: 此言引发了民主党和共和党州长的愤怒回应，其中包括华盛顿州的杰伊·英斯利，他在美国广播公司（ABC）节目中表示：

sentences.en: Well, I think Republicans and Democratic governors were shocked when he said that we should just let the states go bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当他说我们应该任由各州破产时，共和党和民主党州长们都感到震惊。

sentences.en: And I'm trying to think of the right word to describe that, you know, and you might call it ridiculous to say that.
sentences.zh: 我正在想用什么词来形容这种说法，你知道，你可能会说这种言论很荒谬。

sentences.en: You might call it ludicrous, or you might call it McConnell-ish.
sentences.zh: 你可以称之为可笑，或者称之为“麦康奈尔式”的言论。

sentences.en: It's a very McConnell-ish thing to say to let states go bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 让各州破产这种话，确实非常“麦康奈尔”。

sentences.en: It's nuts.
sentences.zh: 这简直是疯了。
